transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Well, they sent me here from work. At the station, I was... I kept moving the airway bags into this specific pattern. I just knew it was the right way to have them, and I was repeating the dispatch numbers out loud while I did it. 

My lieutenant came over and told me to stop and step away, but I wouldn't do it. I couldn't stop, because it felt like the whole bay would go bad if I broke the sequence. So, that's why they made me come see you.
When you felt that the bay would 'go bad' if you broke the sequence, did you feel like that was a logically sound belief, or did you realize that your actions were actually unnecessary?

No, it made complete sense to me. It wasn't unnecessary at all. I... I had to do it, because I know the injury review people and some of the supervisors have been watching me through the station cameras. They've been changing my triage notes to make me look unsafe, even when they tell me it's just routine paperwork. So making sure the bags were set up in the exact right pattern... it was completely logical. I had to do it.
Do you find that your thoughts often become jumbled or that you have trouble keeping track of what you are trying to say?

No, not really. I don't have trouble keeping track of things. My thoughts are actually really clear to me. I know exactly what I'm trying to say, so... no, they don't get jumbled up at all. Everything makes perfect sense in my head.
Do you ever hear voices or sounds that other people around you cannot hear?
No, I don't hear anything like that. I just hear the normal sounds around the station, the dispatch radio... nothing that other people can't hear. Just the regular stuff.
Have you ever considered the possibility that your supervisors are not actually changing your notes or monitoring you through the cameras?

No, I haven't considered that, because I know they are doing it. It's not a possibility, it's just what's happening. I know the injury review people and some of the supervisors are watching me on the station cameras. And I know they're changing my triage notes to make me look like an unsafe EMT. They tell me it's just routine paperwork when they ask about it, but I know what they're actually doing.
How long have you felt that your supervisors have been monitoring you through the cameras and altering your notes?

It's been going on for about the last two months. The camera stuff, the paperwork being changed... all of that started a couple of months ago. And I guess the way I've been handling it at the station is what got everyone so alarmed recently. But yeah, it's been about two months.
Are there any other people, aside from your supervisors, who you believe are involved in this monitoring or interfering with your work?
No, not really. It's... well, it's just the supervisors and the injury review people, like I mentioned. I haven't noticed anyone else getting involved or messing with my stuff. Just them.
During these past two months, have you experienced any significant changes in your mood, such as feeling unusually low or, conversely, feeling exceptionally energetic or invincible?

No, not really. My mood has been pretty normal. I mean, it's obviously stressful dealing with what they're doing to my paperwork at the station, but I haven't felt depressed or... exceptionally energetic, like you said. I'm just my usual self, really, just trying to do my job. So no, no big changes in my mood.
Are there any other specific incidents or details, other than the camera monitoring and paperwork changes, that have led you to believe your supervisors are targeting you?

Um, no... not really. I mean, I haven't noticed anything else. It's just the cameras and them altering my run reports. I haven't seen them do anything else besides that... but honestly, that's more than enough, you know? So, no, just the stuff I already told you about.
Have you noticed any changes in your daily routine, such as difficulties with your personal hygiene, eating habits, or your ability to keep up with your usual responsibilities?

Well, yeah, things have definitely changed. I mean, I can't work the ambulance anymore because of all this. They put me on desk duty, doing notes and equipment checks, but even that... it got so unreliable with them messing with things that they just took me off the schedule completely. So I'm not working right now. And at home... I guess I've mostly stopped seeing my friends. I don't really keep up with things around the house the way I used to, either. It's just hard to focus on that stuff right now.
